newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti warns on ENEL/Deutsche phone bid.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti warns on ENEL/Deutsche phone bid.

text.p: Italy's information and technology group Olivetti on Sunday complained of "dangerous interference" that could be caused by a bid led by Italy's electricity utility company ENEL for Italy's third mobile phone licence.

Olivetti has a controlling 35.5 percent stake in the Omnitel consortium, which since December 1995 has operated Italy's second mobile phone licence, and competes with the number one operator -- state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM).

Last Friday, the Italian Treasury said state-owned ENEL is planning to launch a joint bid with Germany's Deutsche Telekom for Italy's third mobile phone operating licence, in a venture 51 percent owned by ENEL and 49 percent by Deutsche.

Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colaninno told Milan's Corriere della Sera newspaper that Omnitel is already competing with one state-controlled operator, TIM, and that the new bid if successful could see two state operators in the field.
"The entry of ENEL into the market constitutes a serious distortion of competition in the market," he told the paper.

Italy's telecom minister Antonio Maccanico has been reported as saying that the government would invite bids for the third mobile phone licence this month. ENEL is scheduled for privatisation, but the Treasury has set no timetable.
